requirements.title: USE statements specify use association and reference available modules without self-reference
requirements.definition: A USE statement specifies use association, references the named module, requires the public portions of that module to be available at processing time, and a module shall not reference itself directly or indirectly.

pending.use-stmt-specifies-use-association: Define module use_assoc_provider with public integer answer=42; a client USEs it, initializes observed to -777, assigns answer, and expects exact 42.
pending.use-stmt-references-module: Compile provider module before a client containing USE use_assoc_provider; changing only the module name to a different existing module returning -999 changes observed to -999.
pending.module-public-portions-available: Source-control plan builds the provider before the client and records that only public entities are imported; missing-module diagnostics are build-environment evidence, not a portable source oracle here.
pending.module-self-reference-prohibited: Positive source-control uses two acyclic modules with one USE edge. Direct and indirect self-reference mutations change only the USE graph; no diagnostic is required by this unnumbered restriction.

requirements.title: Use association accesses module entities with module attributes and declared or defined status
requirements.definition: A USE statement accesses named data objects, nonintrinsic types, procedures, abstract interfaces, generic identifiers, and namelist groups from a module; the local entities are associated with module entities, have the attributes specified in the module except for separately registered permission exceptions, and variables are previously declared while other entities are previously defined.

pending.use-accesses-named-data-object: Module m exports public integer counter=1; two client modules USE it through separate paths, one subroutine sets counter=42 and the other reads counter into observed initialized to -777, expecting exact 42 to prove same storage.
pending.use-accesses-nonintrinsic-type: Module m exports public type box with integer component; client USEs ONLY box, constructs box(42), and expects component 42 from sentinel -777.
pending.use-accesses-procedure: Module m exports function answer() returning 42; client USEs ONLY answer and expects exact 42 while an external answer sentinel returning -999 would expose wrong resolution.
pending.use-accesses-abstract-interface: Source-control plan exports an abstract interface for a procedure pointer declaration in a client; executable procedure-pointer calls are deferred to Clause 15 procedure-pointer rules.
pending.use-accesses-generic-identifier: Module m exports generic g with integer and real specifics returning exact 31 and 32; client USEs ONLY g and observes g(3)=31 and g(2.0)=32 from sentinels -31 and -32.
pending.use-accesses-namelist-group: Source-control plan exports a public namelist group and a client USEs ONLY the group name; data-transfer execution belongs to Clause 12/13 namelist owners.
pending.use-associated-entity-identity: Module m exports integer shared=5; client USEs m twice through modules a and b, calls set_a(42), then get_b into observed initialized to -777 and expects exact 42, proving both paths designate the same module variable.
pending.use-associated-attributes-preserved: Module m exports PARAMETER p=42 and type box; client USEs p in array bound `integer :: a(p-p+1)` and box in a declaration, proving parameter and type attributes specified in the module survive use association without local redeclaration. Separate accessibility, ASYNCHRONOUS, and VOLATILE permission exceptions are not asserted by this facet.
pending.use-associated-variable-previously-decla: Client USEs module variable shared and assigns it before any local declaration; observed initialized to -777 later reads exact 42. A companion local declaration of shared is a source-control negative owned by p9.
pending.use-associated-nonvariable-previously-de: Client USEs module type box and function answer before local definitions, constructs box(answer()), and expects component 42; external answer sentinel returning -999 exposes wrong resolution.

requirements.title: Use-associated entities may have local accessibility, ASYNCHRONOUS, and VOLATILE attribute exceptions
requirements.definition: An accessed entity may have a different accessibility attribute, may have the ASYNCHRONOUS attribute even without that attribute on the associated module entity, and may have the VOLATILE attribute for a noncoarray entity even without that attribute on the associated module entity.

pending.use-associated-different-accessibility-p: Module provider exports public integer shared=42. Module reexporter USEs provider, ONLY: shared, declares PRIVATE :: shared and PUBLIC :: read_shared, and read_shared returns shared. Client USEs provider directly as original_shared and USEs reexporter ONLY read_shared; observed initialized to -777 expects original_shared + read_shared() == 84. A source-control companion attempts USE reexporter, ONLY: shared and is owned by C1409/private accessibility.
pending.use-associated-asynchronous-permitted: Module provider exports public integer shared=42. Client USEs provider, ONLY: shared, then specifies ASYNCHRONOUS :: shared before executable statements, initializes observed=-777, assigns observed=shared, and expects exact 42; no asynchronous runtime behavior is asserted.
pending.use-associated-volatile-permitted: Module provider exports public noncoarray integer shared=42. Client USEs provider, ONLY: shared, then specifies VOLATILE :: shared before executable statements, initializes observed=-777, assigns observed=shared, and expects exact 42; no optimization-dependent volatile behavior is asserted.

pending.use-defined-binary-operator: Module exports binary OPERATOR(.addbox.); client USEs OPERATOR(.localadd.)=>OPERATOR(.addbox.) and expects exact 207.
pending.invalid-use-defined-operator-rejected: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the module-side operator spelling to intrinsic `OPERATOR(+)` in a defined-operator rename; the repair restores `.addbox.`.

pending.nonintrinsic-module-preferred-over-intri: Source-control plan provides a nonintrinsic module with the same name as an intrinsic module and a distinct public answer=42; a bare USE expects the nonintrinsic entity, while `USE, INTRINSIC ::` names the intrinsic module explicitly.

requirements.definition: For multiple USE statements for a given module, one USE statement without ONLY makes all public entities in the module accessible; an all-ONLY set of USE statements makes entities appearing in one or more only-lists accessible.

pending.all-only-uses-union-only-lists: Client has `use m, only: answer` and `use m, only: bonus`; local noise=-7 shadows unlisted public noise while observed initialized to -777 expects answer+bonus=43.

requirements.title: USE association assigns identifiers from ONLY items, renames, and unrenamed module identifiers
requirements.definition: An accessible module entity is associated with accessed entities identified by listed only-use-names or generic-spec operators, by each local rename, and by the original module identifier absent a rename for that module identifier.

pending.only-use-name-retains-module-identifier: Module m exports answer=42; client USEs ONLY: answer and expects answer gives exact 42.
pending.rename-creates-local-identifier: Module m exports answer=42; client USEs local_answer=>answer, declares local integer answer=-7, and expects local_answer=42 plus local answer=-7.
pending.unrenamed-entity-keeps-module-identifier: Module m exports answer=42 and bonus=1; client USEs m, local_bonus=>bonus. Since answer is unrenamed, observed expects answer+local_bonus=43.
pending.multiple-local-identifiers-same-entity: Client USEs m twice with a=>shared and b=>shared; assigns a=42, then reads b into observed initialized -777 and expects exact 42, proving both identifiers denote the same module variable.

requirements.title: Ultimate-entity conflict rules allow unused identifiers and generic-interface merging
requirements.definition: An ultimate entity is a module entity not accessed by use association. An accessed entity shall not be associated with two or more ultimate entities except for an unused identifier or generic interfaces, with generic interfaces handled by 15.4.3.4.

pending.multiple-ultimate-entity-conflict-prohib: Positive control renames colliding data objects from two modules to distinct local names a and b, expecting exact a+b=83. Source-control mutation imports both as x; no diagnostic is required by this unnumbered restriction.
pending.unused-conflicting-identifier-not-prohib: Source-control control imports two modules that each export x but never uses x, while also importing distinct answer=42; observed expects exact 42 and no claim is made about a used ambiguous x.
pending.generic-interfaces-merge-across-use: Module ma exports generic g for integer returning 31; module mb exports generic g for real returning 32. Client USEs both, initializes results to -777, and expects g(3)=31 plus g(2.0)=32.

requirements.title: Use-associated local identifiers cannot be respecified except allowed accessibility, ASYNCHRONOUS, or VOLATILE attributes
requirements.definition: The local identifier of a use-associated entity shall not appear in another nonexecutable statement that specifies an attribute in the scoping unit, except PUBLIC or PRIVATE in a module and ASYNCHRONOUS or VOLATILE.

pending.use-associated-public-private-exception: Module reexporter USEs provider, ONLY: shared and declares PRIVATE :: shared; downstream client cannot import shared from reexporter, while a public alias still returns exact 42.
pending.use-associated-asynchronous-volatile-exc: Source-control plan USEs module variable shared and specifies VOLATILE :: shared in the client module while reading exact value 42; runtime volatility effects are not asserted.
